body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\eta\le 1/4\). In \(\mathfrak E_3\), the two arrays \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) are nonnegative, have \((D(0),R(1))\) margins \(f^-\) and \(f^+\), have \((D(1),R(1))\) margin \(\mu_1^\star\), and put mass only on \(D(0)\le D(1)\); with \(R(0)=\infty\), each is therefore a feasible full-law lift preserving both displayed within-arm tables. The displayed row sums, column sums, and complete chain-load matrices certify every marked-capacity constraint. The exact coordinate intervals are \(	heta_
u(1,1)\in[1/15,4/15]\), \(	heta_
u(2,2)\in[1/10,1/2]\), and \(	heta_
u(3,3)\in[1/5,4/5]\). For an arbitrary feasible \(f_{ij}\), \(\ell_\star(
u)=f_{10}-f_{21}+f_{30}+f_{32}\), \(\ell_\star(
u)\le f_{10}+f_{30}+f_{32}\le\kappa^\star_{00}+\kappa^\star_{22}=1/4\), while \(f_{21}+f_{31}\le1/10\) and \(f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32}=1/4-f_{33}\ge1/20\) imply \(\ell_\star(
u)\ge-1/20\). The arrays \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) attain these two endpoints, so the sharp interval is \([-1/20,1/4]\), strictly inside the coordinate rectangle \([-3/20,7/20]\). Replacing each finite atom by a sufficiently narrow separated symmetric bump and using a common bump draw when the two death categories agree yields a bounded-Lipschitz law satisfying all maintained conditions with the same strict separation; the separation persists on a relatively open neighborhood.
body.justification: A robust strict example establishes that the joint surface theorem adds identifying content beyond a collection of exact pointwise intervals.
body.gap: Generic warnings that pointwise sharp bounds need not be jointly sharp do not give a legal semicompeting-risk region with binding survivor capacities and exact support certificates.
body.consumer: It tells applied users when horizon-by-horizon uncertainty bands are mathematically incompatible and can reverse conclusions about signed clinical summaries.
body.proof_tex:
The proof is an exact finite-table certificate followed by separated smoothing.  All probabilities are conditional on the sole value of \(X\).  Since \(R(0)=\infty\), the control numerator is \(b(r,t)=0\) at finite \(r\).  The four control death rows each have mass \(1/4\), so
\[
 S(1)=\frac34,\qquad S(2)=\frac12,\qquad S(3)=\frac14.               \tag{18}
\]
Thus \(0<\eta\leq1/4\) places \((1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\) in \(\mathcal H_\eta\), including its boundary.

For a feasible projected table \(f=(f_{ij})\), define
\[
 A_1=\sum_{i>0}f_{i0},\qquad
 A_2=\sum_{\substack{i>1\\j\leq1}}f_{ij},\qquad
 A_3=\sum_{j\leq2}f_{3j}.
\]
The singleton capacities from the quadratic chain theorem and the fixed row demands give
\[
 \frac1{20}\leq A_1\leq\kappa^\star_{00}=\frac15,                  \tag{19}
\]
because the other three first-cut columns have total capacity \(7/10\), while the demand after that cut is \(3/4\).  Similarly,
\[
 \frac1{20}\leq A_2\leq\kappa^\star_{10}+\kappa^\star_{11}
 =\frac14,                                                            \tag{20}
\]
because the second-cut demand is \(1/2\) and columns \(2,3\) have capacity \(9/20\).  Finally,
\[
 \frac1{20}\leq A_3\leq
 \kappa^\star_{20}+\kappa^\star_{21}+\kappa^\star_{22}=\frac15,    \tag{21}
\]
where the lower bound is \(A_3=1/4-f_{33}\geq1/4-\kappa^\star_{23}\).

The upper endpoints in (19)--(21) are attained by the displayed flows \(f^+\), \(f^-\), and \(f^+\), respectively, and the lower endpoint in (21) is attained by \(f^-\).  For the remaining lower endpoints, define
\[
100g^{(1)}=
\begin{pmatrix}
20&0&0&5\\0&15&5&5\\0&0&5&20\\5&5&5&10
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
100g^{(2)}=
\begin{pmatrix}
20&0&0&5\\0&20&0&5\\0&0&10&15\\5&0&5&15
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both have the required row and column margins.  Their complete singleton chain loads are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}5&20&15&35\\5&5&10&30\\5&5&5&10\end{pmatrix}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\begin{pmatrix}5&20&15&35\\5&0&15&30\\5&0&5&15\end{pmatrix},
\]
after multiplication by \(100\); each is entrywise bounded by \(100\kappa^\star\).  The quadratic chain theorem makes both flows feasible, with \(A_1(g^{(1)})=1/20\) and \(A_2(g^{(2)})=1/20\).  Convexity of the finite flow polytope then shows that (19)--(21) are the exact intervals.  Dividing by (18) gives
\[
 \theta_\nu(1,1)\in\left[\frac1{15},\frac4{15}\right],\quad
 \theta_\nu(2,2)\in\left[\frac1{10},\frac12\right],\quad
 \theta_\nu(3,3)\in\left[\frac15,\frac45\right].                  \tag{22}
\]

Direct summation of the listed nonzero lift entries gives
\[
100\left(\sum_hq^-_{ihj}\right)_{ij}
=\begin{pmatrix}10&0&10&5\\0&10&5&10\\15&5&0&5\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix}
=100f^-,
\]
\[
100\left(\sum_hq^+_{ihj}\right)_{ij}
=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&10&10\\10&15&0&0\\0&0&0&25\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix}
=100f^+,
\]
and, for both signs,
\[
100\left(\sum_iq^\pm_{ihj}\right)_{hj}
=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&0&5\\5&10&0&5\\5&5&10&10\\10&5&5&20\end{pmatrix}
=100\mu_1^\star.
\]
Every listed entry is nonnegative.  Both projected tables have row sums \((25,25,25,25)/100\) and column sums \((25,20,15,40)/100\), so attaching \(R(0)=\infty\) gives \(\mu_0^\star\).  Inspection of every positive triple gives \(i\leq h\), hence \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  Every finite treated readmission category in a positive cell satisfies \(r_j^\star<d_h^\star\), while the control event order is vacuous.  The complete singleton chain loads are
\[
100\left(\sum_{i>k}f^-_{ij}\right)_{kj}
=\begin{pmatrix}15&20&5&35\\15&10&0&25\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
100\left(\sum_{i>k}f^+_{ij}\right)_{kj}
=\begin{pmatrix}20&20&5&30\\10&5&5&30\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Comparison with the displayed \(100\kappa^\star\) is entrywise.  Every Borel mark set on this finite carrier is a union of singleton columns, so summing these inequalities certifies all event-set capacities.

Substituting (18) into the signed direction yields
\[
 \ell_\star(\nu)=A_1-A_2+A_3=f_{10}-f_{21}+f_{30}+f_{32}.            \tag{23}
\]
Nonnegativity and the first and third cut capacities give
\[
 \ell_\star(\nu)
 \leq f_{10}+f_{30}+f_{32}
 \leq\kappa^\star_{00}+\kappa^\star_{22}=\frac14.                  \tag{24}
\]
The second-cut capacity in column \(1\) and the last-row margin give
\[
 f_{21}+f_{31}\leq\frac1{10},\qquad
 f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32}=\frac14-f_{33}\geq\frac1{20}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \ell_\star(\nu)
 =f_{10}-(f_{21}+f_{31})+(f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32})
 \geq-\frac1{20}.                                                     \tag{25}
\]
Direct substitution gives \(\ell_\star(f^-)=-1/20\) and \(\ell_\star(f^+)=1/4\).  The verified full lifts attain both values, and mixtures of them preserve the fixed margins, monotonicity, and event order.  Hence the sharp signed interval is \([-1/20,1/4]\).

If the three coordinates in (22) could vary independently, the same direction would instead have endpoints
\[
 \frac34\frac1{15}-\frac12\frac12+\frac14\frac15=-\frac3{20},
 \qquad
 \frac34\frac4{15}-\frac12\frac1{10}+\frac14\frac45=\frac7{20}.
\]
Thus the coordinate rectangle has support \([-3/20,7/20]\), strictly larger by \(1/10\) at each endpoint.

For smoothing, choose a nonnegative symmetric continuously differentiable density \(\varphi_\delta\) of integral one supported on \((-\delta,\delta)\), where \(0<\delta<1/8\).  Replace every finite category by the corresponding translated bump and retain \(\infty\).  Conditional on a positive categorical lift cell \((i,h,j)\), use independent death bumps when \(i<h\), the same death draw when \(i=h\), and an independent readmission bump.  Adjacent death centers are one unit apart, so this preserves \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  The smallest finite gap between a compatible treated readmission center and death center is \(1/4\), and \(2\delta<1/4\) therefore preserves \(R(1)<D(1)\).  Finite-part within-arm densities are finite mixtures of translates and products of \(\varphi_\delta\), so they have finite sup-norm and Lipschitz constants and meet the audited envelopes whenever those constants are chosen as the corresponding model bounds.

No bump support crosses any threshold \(1,2,3\).  All numerators, denominators, and capacities used in (19)--(25) therefore retain their categorical values.  Applying the same bump kernels under the two signs preserves their common smoothed within-arm margins, while the two projected couplings retain the two signed endpoints.  The exact support calculations thus remain valid for bounded-Lipschitz witnesses.

Finally fix the separated kernels and incidence pattern and vary the finitely many mixture weights inside the feasible cone.  After slack variables are introduced, the support programs have a fixed finite constraint matrix and finitely many bases.  On every basis region the optimal value is affine in the weights, and values agree where optimality regions meet; hence every endpoint is continuous and piecewise affine.  Both strict gaps equal \(1/10\) at the displayed law, so they remain positive on a sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood.  The randomized treatment \(e=1/2\), degenerate positive covariate cell, consistency, and \(C=\tau=3\) additionally give exchangeability, overlap, and \(G_{zx}(u)=1\geq\gamma\) through the full horizon.
